findings.source_quote: Περίζωσαι ὠμόλινον, | καὶ διακόνει μοι. καὶ περιεζωσάμην ὠμόλινον | ἐκ σάκκου γεγονὸς καθαρόν.
findings.english_quote: “Put on a garment of unfinished linen and serve me.” So I put on a clean garment of unfinished linen made from sackcloth.
findings.issue: The command and its fulfillment both specify girding oneself with the linen article, not merely putting on a garment. The later phrase “fastened up my clothing” does not clearly recover the action of tying this article around the waist.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed wording for fresh review: “Tie a piece of raw linen around your waist and serve me.” So I tied around my waist a clean piece of raw linen made from a sack.

findings.source_quote: τινὲς δὲ χλωρὰς καὶ παραφυάδας ἐχούσας, καὶ εἰς τὰς παραφυάδας καρπούς, οἵους εἶχον οἱ εἰς τὸν πύργον πορευθέντες ἐστεφανωμένοι
findings.english_quote: Some rods were green and had shoots bearing fruit, like the rods held by the crowned people who had gone into the tower.
findings.issue: The source explicitly compares the fruit with the fruit the crowned people had: οἵους agrees with καρπούς. The simplified text instead compares rods and adds that the crowned people held them. This loses the specific fruit comparison and introduces an unsupported physical action.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed wording for fresh review: “Some handed in green rods with shoots bearing fruit like the fruit the crowned people who had gone into the tower had.”

summary: The standard edition faithfully covers the supplied working Greek, including the rod conditions, negations, commands, and group assignments; its bracketed nouns transparently mark English supplements. Independent review of the simplified edition identifies two local fidelity defects concerning girding and the fruit comparison. No alternative readings or manuscript reports were supplied, and this review does not authenticate unseen witnesses. Proposed corrections require fresh review.
